title: Joshua 20:4–6 (the elders' hearing at the gate) — absent from Brenton’s Greek
summary: KJV Joshua 20:4–6 gives the procedure at the city gate and the stay until the high priest’s death. The Hebrew has these verses; Brenton’s Greek of chapter 20 has no text for verses 4, 5 and 6.
text: KJV Joshua 20:4–6: “And when he that doth flee unto one of those cities shall stand at the entering of the gate of the city, and shall declare his cause in the ears of the elders of that city, they shall take him into the city unto them, and give him a place, that he may dwell among them. And if the avenger of blood pursue after him, then they shall not deliver the slayer up into his hand; because he smote his neighbour unwittingly, and hated him not beforetime. And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment, and until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days: then shall the slayer return, and come unto his own city, and unto his own house, unto the city from whence he fled.” Hebrew (WLC) Joshua 20:4–6: וְנָ֞ס אֶל־אַחַ֣ת ׀ מֵהֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְעָמַד֙ פֶּ֚תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֔יר וְדִבֶּ֛ר בְּאָזְנֵ֛י זִקְנֵ֥י הָעִֽיר־הַהִ֖יא אֶת־דְּבָרָ֑יו וְאָסְפ֨וּ אֹתֹ֤ו הָעִ֙ירָה֙ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְנָתְנוּ־לֹ֥ו מָקֹ֖ום וְיָשַׁ֥ב עִמָּֽם׃ וְכִ֨י יִרְדֹּ֜ף גֹּאֵ֤ל הַדָּם֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וְלֹֽא־יַסְגִּ֥רוּ אֶת־הָרֹצֵ֖חַ בְּיָדֹ֑ו כִּ֤י בִבְלִי־דַ֙עַת֙ הִכָּ֣ה אֶת־רֵעֵ֔הוּ וְלֹֽא־שֹׂנֵ֥א ה֛וּא לֹ֖ו מִתְּמֹ֥ול שִׁלְשֹֽׁום׃ וְיָשַׁ֣ב ׀ בָּעִ֣יר הַהִ֗יא עַד־עָמְדֹ֞ו לִפְנֵ֤י הָֽעֵדָה֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט עַד־מֹות֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּדֹ֔ול אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֑ם אָ֣ז ׀ יָשׁ֣וּב הָרֹוצֵ֗חַ וּבָ֤א אֶל־עִירֹו֙ וְאֶל־בֵּיתֹ֔ו אֶל־הָעִ֖יר אֲשֶׁר־נָ֥ס מִשָּֽׁם׃ [… 20:4–6 as in the KJV: the slayer states his case to the elders at the gate, is not handed to the avenger, and stays until trial and the death of the high priest.] Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Joshua 20:3 and 20:7, the verses either side of the gap: Φυγαδευτήριον τῷ φονευτῇ τῷ πατάξαντι ψυχὴν ἀκουσίως· καὶ ἔσονται ὑμῖν αἱ πόλεις φυγαδευτήριον, καὶ οὐκ ἀποθανεῖται ὁ φονευτὴς ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγχιστεύοντος τὸ αἷμα, ἕως ἂν καταστῇ· ἐναντίον τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰς κρίσιν. title: Ephraim “went northward” (Judges 12:1) — the Greek has a place, “Boraran”
summary: KJV Judges 12:1 says the men of Ephraim “went northward”. The Hebrew word is צָפֹונָה (tsaphonah); the Greek prints the place name Βοῤῥᾶν instead of a direction.

[… and a man of Ephraim cried out, and they passed over to Borran, and they said to Jephthah …] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JDG12.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/7/12/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JDG12.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew word can be read as a direction (“to the north”) or as the place Zaphon. The KJV takes the direction; the Greek has a name.

title: Micah pays the Levite “by the year” (Judges 17:10) — the Greek has “a day”
summary: KJV Judges 17:10 gives the Levite ten shekels of silver “by the year”. The Hebrew is לַיָּמִים (lit. “for the days”); the Greek prints δέκα ἀργυρίου εἰς ἡμέραν, “ten of silver for a day”.
text: KJV Judges 17:10: “And Micah said unto him, Dwell with me, and be unto me a father and a priest, and I will give thee ten shekels of silver by the year, and a suit of apparel, and thy victuals. So the Levite went in.” Hebrew (WLC) Judges 17:10: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לֹ֨ו מִיכָ֜ה שְׁבָ֣ה עִמָּדִ֗י וֶֽהְיֵה־לִי֮ לְאָ֣ב וּלְכֹהֵן֒ וְאָנֹכִ֨י אֶֽתֶּן־לְךָ֜ עֲשֶׂ֤רֶת כֶּ֙סֶף֙ לַיָּמִ֔ים וְעֵ֥רֶךְ בְּגָדִ֖ים וּמִחְיָתֶ֑ךָ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הַלֵּוִֽי׃ [… ten (of) silver for the days, and an order of garments, and your keep.] Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Judges 17:10: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Μιχαίας, κάθου μετʼ ἐμοῦ, καὶ γίνου μοι εἰς πατέρα καὶ εἰς ἱερέα, καὶ ἐγὼ δώσω σοι δέκα ἀργυρίου εἰς ἡμέραν, καὶ στολὴν ἱματίων, καὶ τὰ πρὸς ζωήν σου. [… ten (of) silver for a day, and a robe of garments, and what is for your living.] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JDG17.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/7/17/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JDG17.htm.

title: “The LORD hath testified against me” (Ruth 1:21) — the Greek has “the Lord humbled me”
summary: KJV Ruth 1:21 renders וַיהוָה עָנָה בִי as “the LORD hath testified against me”. The Greek prints Κύριος ἐταπείνωσέ με, “the Lord humbled me”.
text: KJV Ruth 1:21: “I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty: why then call ye me Naomi, seeing the LORD hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me?” Hebrew (WLC) Ruth 1:21: אֲנִי֙ מְלֵאָ֣ה הָלַ֔כְתִּי וְרֵיקָ֖ם הֱשִׁיבַ֣נִי יְהוָ֑ה לָ֣מָּה תִקְרֶ֤אנָה לִי֙ נָעֳמִ֔י וַֽיהוָה֙ עָ֣נָה בִ֔י וְשַׁדַּ֖י הֵ֥רַֽע לִֽי׃ [… and the LORD has ‘anah in me (answered/testified against me, or afflicted me) …] Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ruth 1:21: Ἐγὼ πλήρης ἐπορεύθην, καὶ κενὴν ἀπέστρεψέ με ὁ Κύριος· καὶ ἱνατί καλεῖτέ με Νωεμὶν, καὶ Κύριος ἐταπείνωσέ με, καὶ ὁ ἱκανὸς ἐκάκωσέ με; [… and the Lord has humbled me, and the Sufficient One has treated me ill.] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/RUT01.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/8/1/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/RUT01.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew verb עָנָה can be read as “answer, testify” or as “afflict, humble”; the KJV takes the first, the Greek the second. In the Hebrew, Naomi’s next clause (“Shaddai has done me harm”) already says harm, so the clause is either a charge of testimony or a second statement of affliction.
scope: T applies at Ruth 1:21 only and compares how one Hebrew verb is taken. Without a lexicon opened here this record does not say which sense is correct; it only records that the Greek and KJV read the verb differently and that the KJV’s “testified against” carries a courtroom picture that the Greek “humbled” does not. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.
